raw_response:
I farm 8 mu, so I will not spread money everywhere the same way. I will first hold onto the wheat-maize ground, because that is the steady grain for the house and the safest income. On my land, grain is what I cannot afford to lose, so I will feed wheat and maize a bit heavier than the cash crops. I have well water, so I will use it when the crop is at the key stage, not just wait for the sky. I went to primary school, so I do pay attention to things like base fertilizer, topdressing, and whether the plants are short or pale, but in the end I still do what has worked on fields around me. If neighbors get good wheat ears and full maize cobs from improved or hybrid seed, I will follow that. For cotton, I will not make the area too big, because labor and spraying are troublesome, but I will still keep some because if the stand is even and insects are controlled, it can still bring cash. Watermelon costs more up front, but if I manage water and disease well, one small piece can make money fast, so I will keep some area there too. I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than let the crop sit hungry, because losing yield hurts more than wasting one small bit of input.
